workflows.title: Effect clips from a photo
workflows.what: Turns a photo into a 5 second effect clip: cakeify, hydraulic press, explode, inflate, squish, 360 degree orbit, crane up, crash zoom, dolly zoom.

source.credit: neuregex/ComfyUI-freefield, a snapshot of the Freefield apps (MIT)

workflows.tested: Not run on a 24 GB card upstream. Measured peak: 41.94 GB on H100 · 20261023-162024-h100.

inputs.name: subject
inputs.about: A few words on who or what is in the photo.

cakeify.value: The video opens on {subject}. A knife, held by a hand, is coming into frame and hovering over it. The knife then begins cutting into it to c4k3 cakeify it. As the knife slices it open, the inside is revealed to be cake with chocolate layers. The knife cuts through and the contents are revealed. {details}

crush.value: The video begins with {subject}. A hydraulic press positioned above slowly descends towards it. Upon contact, the hydraulic press c5us4 crushes it, deforming and flattening it, causing it to collapse inward until it is no longer recognizable. {details}

explode.value: The video opens with {subject}. Then it 3xp105ion huge explosion that engulfs the entire screen with a bright light. The light is so bright that it obscures everything around. {details}

inflate.value: The video shows {subject}, then infl4t3 inflates it, expanding into a giant, round, inflated figure. {details}

squish.value: In the video, {subject} is presented, held in a person's hands. The person then presses on it, causing a sq41sh squish effect. The person keeps pressing down on it, further showing the sq41sh squish effect. {details}

orbit-360.value: The video shows {subject}. The camera performs an 0rb4it 360 degree orbit, circling around and showing the surroundings, before returning to the front view. Throughout the 0rb4it 360 degree orbit, the main subject stays in place. {details}

crane-up.value: The video shows {subject}. The cr4n3 crane up effect is applied, smoothly lifting the camera's viewpoint higher, revealing more of the surrounding landscape. {details}

crash-zoom-in.value: The video shows {subject}. The camera performs a cr34sh crash zoom in effect, rapidly zooming closer to the face. {details}

dolly-zoom.value: dolly zoom. The video shows {subject}. The camera moves toward them while zooming out: they stay the same size and the background behind them stretches away. {details}

orbit_left.value: The video shows {subject}. The camera performs an 0rb4it 360 degree orbit, circling around and showing the surroundings, before returning to the front view. Throughout the 0rb4it 360 degree orbit, the main subject stays in place. {details}

orbit_right.value: The video shows {subject}. The camera performs an 0rb4it 360 degree orbit, circling around and showing the surroundings, before returning to the front view. Throughout the 0rb4it 360 degree orbit, the main subject stays in place. {details}

crane_up.value: The video shows {subject}. The cr4n3 crane up effect is applied, smoothly lifting the camera's viewpoint higher, revealing more of the surrounding landscape. {details}

push_in.value: The video shows {subject}. The camera performs a cr34sh crash zoom in effect, rapidly zooming closer to the face. {details}

dolly_zoom.value: dolly zoom. The video shows {subject}. The camera moves toward them while zooming out: they stay the same size and the background behind them stretches away. {details}

workflows.title: Re-angle a video
workflows.what: Re-shoots a clip from a new camera angle: it lifts the footage into depth, moves the camera, and lets LTX-2.5 paint what the move reveals. Small moves (10 to 20 degrees) work best.
workflows.tested: Upstream ran it on an RTX 5080 (16 GB), peak about 15.3 GB, about 55 s a chunk. Only the 16 GB tier is measured. Do not use the Base or Large depth models: they are non-commercial.

inputs.name: prompt

inputs.about: What the scene is, so the filled-in parts match.

workflows.title: Lip sync: say new words in a clip
workflows.what: Makes the person in a clip say new words, in any language: a new voice track and new lip movement from your text (an LTX-2.5 DubIt LoRA).

source.credit: neuregex/ComfyUI-freefield, a snapshot of the Freefield apps (MIT)

workflows.tested: Ran its example without an error on an RTX 3090 Ti (24 GB) on 2026-11-05, about 135 s (upstream's own test, not ours). It fits a 24 GB card only with plenty of system memory (upstream had 104 GB).
